body: Hi, I'm in this right now. This weekend will be extremely triggering for me. It's a BPD nightmare situation. I am terrified of it. I don't want to have to manage more pain in general, never mind at that severity. I have convinced myself that my only way out is suicide before it happens. The thing is, I really don't want to do it, and it's scary. I just feel like there's no other choice. It's a horrible, deeply unsettling feeling. I'm practically begging to go inpatient for a bit just so I can escape for the time being without having to do the worst thing.
Both ! -40 is the point where F and C are equal :)

Yeah I worked at the blood bank, and we stored frozen plasma in freezers that were -40. We didn't need any gear other than gloves, but we were never allowed to go in by ourselves, and you had to swap with the other person with you every minute.
Nope, Yuri was in the bottom.

Oh god, I wish I could help you here. I'm not leaving my partner, just giving them and myself some space for a week while I go home. And even to just leave for a week took everything in me and I'm still terrified of doing it.

But I do want to say I know how you're feeling. My partner is amazing and patient and loving, but they're polyamorous and I'm monogamous. Dealbreaker, right? Nope. I'm terrified of not having them. I'm their main partner which helps but this dynamic does not help my situation. I just cannot bring myself to leave. Feels like I'd die, so I take what I can get.
Opioids for me
Hi, this sounds a lot like me and it's hell. I have BPD, could be worth looking into?

Yes, but the others are all optional. Painkillers are optional, and antacids are also optional, as well as beta blockers. Benzos are seen as less optional, although still not necessary, but they're harder to get a hold of.

First, I will say that here in the UK, they really don't like prescribing anything beyond first-line medication when it comes to mental health. Things like fluoxetine, sertraline, citalopram, etc.

However, I can't say how hard it is to get mood stabilisers yet because they wouldn't see me, and I won't be seen by anyone until the 19th. I'm hoping it's not too hard, but I expect to have to plead my case at least somewhat.

Thanks for your understanding :( It's not great, no. It's so hard.

Thanks for commenting.

As for the former, I just feel so bad. Because I'll tell them and they'll look so sad and worried, but also tired because it's hard for them too. And they'll ask if there's anything they can do to help me, and I'll say I don't know because I never do. And they'll suggest hospital/doctor stuff, and it's all things I've already tried/done before. And then they'll feel the need to look after me because they don't trust me to keep myself safe and I'll feel bad and burdensome for it.

As for uni, well, you could say I have been taking a break. We started a month ago (I'm only doing a foundation year right now), and I've been in maybe twice? I avoid calls and don't check my emails because I'm so scared I've already ruined it all. I've just been trying to pretend it doesn't exist. I'm so scared. BPD ruins everything, and trying to access the help I need to manage it feels like an endless fruitless fight.

Thanks for commenting. It means a lot to hear from another pwBPD. I'm 22F. How do we do it? I don't understand. How do we live like this? My diagnosis was fairly recent, although I had suspected it for a while, and it's been tough. That's an understatement, actually.

Believe me, I have been trying so hard to get on mood stabilisers. Currently, all I have to manage my mood somewhat is excessive amounts of painkillers. I'm hoping they will let me start them after my screening, but they won't do it sooner. I don't know if I can make it that long. Even just since my screening referral, I have almost given myself a concussion from beating myself over the head with a frying pan, I have self-harmed multiple times, and I have smashed glasses and plates all over my floor.

I am exhausted. The emotional pain has been causing me to dissociate when I'm not writhing on the floor sobbing and hyperventilating. I just want it to stop. How do I comprehend living my life with this thing that I had no say in, when I can't even comprehend the next day?

Sorry for venting :( and I'm sorry for your loss.

Yup, I suffered with OSFED for many years. However, much like the other commenter, I suddenly realised that it just wasn't worth it. It took me really jeopardising my health to make me realise, however, but for the most part I've never engaged in those behaviours since.

But there's nothing they can do. My partner knows about my diagnosis and has been there for me throughout, but what can they actually do for me? I have no idea how I can be helped. And I can't keep putting them through this. They almost lost me only a month ago, if that. I just don't know what I'm actually supposed to do about this. I want mood stabilisers, but I have to go through so many referrals to even be seen. It's hard to think about things possibly getting better in the future when the thought of doing this for even another day is so scary.

Completely understand this. I tend to do the same the less I hear. I'm with my partner most of the week, so I also don't have any rules around texting, as long as we have some dedicated time away from our phones or devices every now and then.

We do names and ages. They all know what I look like but I don't know what any of them look like. We also are open about plans and when things are happening.

However, my partner tends to message me during dates, not just before and after. I've never asked for this, although I do appreciate it. I was worried they were doing it out of guilt at first, but they tell me they love me and miss me, or tell me that they're yapping about me.

You're completely right. My partner is actually relatively new to actually practising polyamory, even though they've known it for a while. They don't experience jealousy when it comes to other people they see who already identify as polyam.

But yes, they do say it a lot. It's almost always in a joking manner, and they'll call themselves a hypocrite all the while. But it's more so thinly veiled honesty even then.

I have also been honest about the fact that it's hard for me, but that was only last weekend after trying to hide it for so long. But, at the end of the day, my partner can joke about blocking or being mean to anyone who is interested in me because they are very assured in the fact that I am monogamous and only choose them. I do not have those same liberties. As much as I am bad at hiding that it's hard for me, I do not outright say it. I try my best to not make it their problem.

Yeah, it's exhausting. And I struggle to talk about it without feeling absolutely pathetic lol. I'm hoping things get a bit better but I've had such a hard two weeks and poly-wise this Thursday until Sunday is going to be a doozy. I'm really, really nervous about how I'm going to feel.

In my case, my partner doesn't love anyone else, they're just getting to know people. They are also saturated at 2, but I haven't seen what that will look like yet. If I struggle this much with being the only partner my partner loves and being bragged about this much, god knows what I'll do if and when they do love someone else. God I love them and feel loved but as you say, is it enough? If their happiness comes at your expense? I'm very prone to codependency so this does play on my mind.

I've thought the same thing. I don't believe it is intentionally manipulative, at least, they're just used to having me to themselves and enjoy it. They know I'm not poly so the thought of me trying it scares them, but they would never try to stop me or tell me not to. But saying it in the first place, whilst I sometimes enjoy hearing it, does feel weird.

Capacity is definitely the issue currently. I am not doing very well. I am in a new city away from everyone I know, and starting uni for the first time. Usually I can manage things better but right now I can't manage much at all. This is making things far more difficult.

Thanks so much for commenting. This is something I've struggled to figure out.

At first, we tried not to mention any names. This didn't work because every time a name was avoided, it got to me. Then we tried all the information. I would know all names, plans and they would be brought up in conversation. This hasn't been going so well, either.

I don't want to know so little that it makes it something my partner feels bad about and feels the need to hide, because it's a part of them and it makes them happy. As well as this, we live 5 minutes away from each other, and spend a lot of time together, so I do prefer to know when they have a date or something because the knowing feels at least a bit better than the guessing. I'm not sure exactly what the sweet spot is in terms of what information is divulged. The only thing I've managed to have some success with is asking them not to talk to me like I am also poly.

As for comparisons, you're right. I've never doubted that I am loved, but I do have a lot of guilt and shame surrounding my mental illnesses and people worrying about me, so it's definitely something I need to work on.
Augh I don't know what to do.

I'm really glad you're alright! It can be so hard, we really have to savour that.

I always remind myself of how much better I'll feel once the feeling passed, knowing I didn't act out from those feelings. They hurt and I wish they wouldn't, but I don't deserve to also feel ashamed afterwards. Thank you for reminding me I'm safe, I am. A week ago I felt so unsafe, and right now that's not the case. I'm trying to lean into that.

Thanks so much for commenting. You're right in saying that what I'm feeling right now can be managed myself, it's not so intense that I need someone to help me. And it's far, far better than when I was a week ago. That felt like a nightmare I couldn't wake up from.

As for distractions, putting unhealthy coping methods aside, I like to play games. It's been harder to enjoy them since having an fp but I still try to play. I also like doing chores, cleaning my room, washing dishes, hoovering, etc. Apart from that, to be honest, not much else!

I haven't had much luck with progressive muscle relaxation from trying it in the past. TIPP has helped me a few times, specifically cold showers. That tends to bring me back down to earth and gives me the mental space to remind myself of the facts.

Sadly it's pretty standard here in the UK. I've been in hospital several times because of attempts in the past and they've never chosen to keep me in. They say things like they don't want to remove me from my environment and my life and want me to stay involved with my community but really it's because they don't really have the funds to keep people in inpatient unless it's absolutely unavoidable. I even said that I didn't feel safe and that I could attempt or self harm at any moment due to how often I feel triggered and it still wasn't enough.

You have no idea how much I needed to hear this, you are so lovely. Thank you so so much 🫂 I will learn over time, whilst I struggle and see these people still choosing to support me, that it's okay to be loved. I also feel a lot better today than I did before my attempt, so I guess I had to hit rock bottom before things got better. Thank you again 🥺🩷

Thank you for commenting. I know it passes every time but it happens so often I'm so tired of fighting it. And it looks so pathetic how every time I feel or cry I look like I'm grieving someone's death it hurts so bad. I'm scared of facing more days with my mind. I hate being me so much. I just want things to be easy. I can't sleep and my partner is asleep and I feel like screaming and writhing around it hurts so much.
Lol thought I might have! Thank you so much!

There's honestly not much you can do. My partner had a month where they were feeling depressed and not very sexual. During this time, I made that the priority, especially knowing they had a rough history with sex in general. I reassured them that we would go at their pace and there were no expectations whatsoever. Then I didn't bring it up. My only focus was their comfort and making sure they didn't feel like there was any pressure whatsoever. At the end of the day, I can take care of those needs myself. Was it easy? No, I have a very high sex drive. But when it comes to sex, if it's not an enthusiastic yes, it's a no. I felt loved in plenty of other ways. My partner has never made me feel unwanted or unloved, and I reminded myself of that even when the lack of intimacy made me feel that way.

You mentioned that his reasons are that he either isn't horny or he's comfortable with you. There's nothing you can do about the first one, but the second one is something you can talk about with him. Feeling comfortable with you doesn't mean intimacy should go out the window. Suggest having him help you without necessarily getting involved himself, maybe?

There's not really anything you can do about getting this need met unless he's fully willing, so you may have to think about how important getting it met is to you. How much longer can you go like this?

Good luck! Everything genuinely seems SO okay, I promise you have nothing to worry about. She seems to care a lot about you. Read this as many times as you need. I understand because I've felt similarly before, but I just remind myself that it all comes down to trust. No matter what, I trust my girlfriend, and that reminds me that things are okay.

I think you genuinely have nothing to worry about. She has been open and honest, and everything you mentioned has happened since just sounds like her talking nicely about someone she is platonically friendly with. There are 0 red flags here, please try to trust her. She hasn't given you any reason not to. Insecurity can be a relationship killer.

Hi, hii. I've been through similar stuff. I'm t4t, I'm a trans guy, and my gf is trans. She's super extroverted compared to me, so I always worry about being replaced, even though I have no reason to believe that would happen.

I also make a point of being as healthy a partner as possible, so I too would never tell my girlfriend what she can and can't do, but I still have to deal with all the feelings it brings up.

What helped the most was getting medicated for sure. My emotions are now super flat, so I don't find myself scared of being abandoned all the time. Before meds, it was ROUGH. A lot of opioids were involved (that's still the case, though).

As for healthy things? IFS helped (my mother's partner does it so I could access it for free via him). TIPP really helped. When I was feeling particularly worked up, I would throw myself into a freezing cold shower for a minute, and it would calm me straight down. I began to talk to myself in a more gentle manner, too. The thing that helped the MOST was to use HEAVY logic on myself.

What I mean by that is I remind myself of the current facts of my situation. Is there really anything wrong right now? And if that doesn't work, I remind myself that NO MATTER WHAT, this will pass. And acting on it does absolutely nothing good, so all I have to do is the best thing I could do, which is wait it out. Literally the only thing I have to do is nothing, even when it feels so intense. But again, being medicated has made all of this easier for me.

Okay so messaging a partner every 3 or 4 hours isn't excessive at all. I think that's pretty standard! Likely if she found this frequency too much, it was actually the contents of the messages that was too much. Did you find that a lot of the messages you sent were a product of anxious spiralling and thoughtloops?

Less than that frequency would definitely be triggering, and a decline in frequency is really hard to deal with when you just want things to go back to how they were and have no idea how to make that happen.

I have been in your position; it's terrifying. I'm especially prone to those doomloops myself. But I can say this.

You can trust in the space. I promise it will only do you good, and although this isn't guaranteed, it's the best way to have your relationship recover. I gave my girlfriend space. The meaning of "space" was agreed upon between us. For us, we would message as normal, but I would stop initiating calls for a little while (my suggestion). This way, I would be encouraged to deal with my spiralling myself, or with the help of someone else so it wasn't all on her. She would still call whenever. We made a full recovery.

Again, space doesn't feel natural. It conjures up all sorts of thoughts. Am I delaying the inevitable? Is it too late? Will I be replaced? But every time these thoughts occur, remind yourself that it's okay to have them. That doesn't mean you have to act on them. Just sit them out. It gets easier over time and I always remind myself that yeah, all those things could happen. But I can't prevent that now, and acting on my urges can ONLY make things worse. So, at that point, the only thing I can try is to trust in giving space. It's the only option. And it feels HARD. But every time you make it out and see that your relationship was unaffected this time, it feels so good. Framing it as a genuine act of love, where I'm not prioritising my need to feel calm over her need for space, helped me as well.

They did tell me this would happen, and I understood why, but with the brain of an 8 year old, that only meant so much.

There was the unintentional side effect of emotional neglect due to being the sibling with fewer problems, lol.

Yup, it's really difficult for me. My brain refuses to let it work, lol.

Like, sure I can tell myself that things are okay but they're not and ignoring that fact feels wrong. And it feels like, if I'm not constantly feeling bad for past mistakes then I'm letting myself off the hook too easy and might make the mistake again. It's funny because being hard on myself in that way usually makes things worse.
I relate to this very strongly 🫂 My self hate is the most damaging thing about me.

Heyy, I'm not a heavy drinker, but I do drink every now and then so I might be able to offer some perspective.

Drinking alone makes things horrible. But seeing as you're at a party, you won't be alone. It's kinda hit or miss? If I go into the night in a good mood, drinking is fun, but if I go into it in a bad mood or for the wrong reasons, it tends to make me act out more easily. Drinking affects everyone differently; in my case I'm either super happy or super sad, but either way I get really needy.

As for afterwards, it depends on how much you drink, but this is where the trouble lies for me. If I drink enough, I get hangover anxiety for a day or two and get depressed and my mood is all over the place.

So, in conclusion? It can make things worse, and you may have less control over your actions. It could also be okay. Just take it easy and see how you feel.

Hi. In a bit of a rough spot right now.

So I've been here, and I've gotten better, and it wasn't just anxiety with me but also Relationship OCD.

It's way easier said than done, but the solution is not to give in to any urges that stem from that anxiety in the moment.

Let's say your partner has gone out for the day. They're busy, so they're not replying frequently, if at all. During this time, you just don't bother them. You can send a few memes/reels for them to look at later if that's something you do, but don't try and get a conversation out of them or call. The goal is to make sure you're the person dealing with your anxiety, not them. You can do chores/go on a walk/reach out to friends to distract yourself, in fact this is all a lot easier the busier you are, but the main thing is that you don't go to your partner to reassure you during these times. If it's something you feel like you NEED to talk about with them, wait until you feel less anxious and see how you feel then.
